selected_on: Regime B (archived lead-1 forecast weather) mean validation MAE
selection_rationale: Regime A is a reanalysis benchmark and is not reproducible on any real forecast evening, so the operational regime decides. The quantile residual head replaced the mean-targeting one because MAE is minimised by the conditional median, not the mean, and the previous champion carried a -69.6 MW bias.

serving_notes.target_parameterisation: Model predicts tn_peak_demand_mw directly. Do NOT add an anchor. Adding peak_lag_1 would roughly double the forecast.
serving_notes.lag_representation: peak_lag_N / energy_lag_N are LITERAL calendar offsets (T-N), as produced by load_phase5_data and build_dataset.add_lags. Do NOT apply config.H_BY_GROUP shifts when serving: load_master(H=2) shifts the demand block one further day, so its 'peak_lag_2' holds T-3 and its 'peak_lag_7' lands on the wrong weekday. H=2 is honoured by EXCLUDING peak_lag_1 and energy_lag_1, not by shifting.

honest_estimates.method: hyperparameters re-selected on inner folds 2023/2024 only, 2025 scored once - see run_phase7_surge.py honest_validation and run_selection_audit.py

known_limitations: Surge-day bias is reduced but NOT solved: on untouched 2025 the inner-selected quantile level cuts surge |bias| by only 7%. A global quantile shift cannot fix a conditional problem - see results/phase7_surge.json.
Recency weighting was tested across half-lives 1-8 years and is not adopted; it is redundant with the trend feature and Ridge extrapolation - see results/phase7_recency.json.
A4_festival reduces Diwali bias +1,519 -> +259 MW but its overall gain does not clear the paired-CI bar on this cell; it is reported as an extension, not adopted.
note_2026: 2026 has NOT been used in tuning or selection. It was inspected during Track A diagnostics, so it is a confirmation set, not a blind test.
